tasks.short: Answer staff questions on curriculum and programme rules, meet teachers to advise on curriculum development, write advice guides, check them, publish them on the staff portal, and demonstrate materials and equipment.

steps.what: Instructional coordinator answers staff questions on programmes and procedures by e-mail
Instructional coordinator advises teaching staff in curriculum development
Instructional coordinator writes advice guides on programme rules and use of materials

loop.input: The coordinator's notes and the current texts of the programme rules and procedures.
loop.output: A draft guide for staff with a reference to the rule behind each point.
loop.check: Code checks every reference points to a paragraph that exists in the current rule texts; points without a valid reference are dropped. The coordinator reads each point against its paragraph: does the paragraph say what the point says; points that do not match are rewritten.
loop.stop: Stops when all references resolve and the coordinator approves, or after two failed redrafts the coordinator writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules must be explained in plain terms for teachers; a list of rule texts does not do that.

steps.what: Instructional coordinator checks the final guide: each point matches the current rule text it cites and the guide answers the questions staff ask
Instructional coordinator publishes the checked guide: by e-mail to staff today, by one release on the staff portal after the change
Instructional coordinator demonstrates use of materials and equipment to staff

tasks.design: Published guides and a staff FAQ on the staff portal ({DOCS}) answer routine questions about programme rules and materials, so fewer questions come by e-mail. A bounded step drafts guides from the coordinator's notes and the current rule texts; code checks every reference, and the coordinator edits. The coordinator checks the final guide and releases it once on the portal. Advising teachers and demonstrating equipment stay with the coordinator. No pupil data go into the drafting step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each question was answered by e-mail and guides written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Staff portals hold guides; language models draft text from notes with checked references.
tasks.still_hard: Rules change and guides go out of date.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a sceptical team see why a new programme is worth the effort.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator edits guides and answers harder questions.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft guides from notes, with references checked against source texts by code.
Kennisnet advises schools to put no personal data in AI tools, with a processor agreement and a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff questions to equipment demonstrated; curriculum decisions are outside.
Input contract: current rule texts kept by the school office; fallback is e-mail answers.
Advising and demonstrating do not change.
Teachers look up the portal in about the time an e-mail took.

incremental.description: Instructional coordinator keeps the FAQ current.

approvals.approved_version: The guide exactly as checked by the coordinator in s4, published once on the staff portal's guide page; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: staff keep e-mailing most questions and drafts need heavy edits (s1 85, s3 80) (11.7); high: the FAQ answers routine questions as assumed (22.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach students, advise them individually, prepare lesson materials, and answer students' questions.

steps.what: Instructional coordinator teaches students
Instructional coordinator advises students individually
Instructional coordinator prepares lesson materials

loop.input: The lesson objectives and the existing slides for the topic.
loop.output: Draft slides and exercises at the group's level.
loop.check: Code checks every exercise maps to a lesson objective code. The coordinator reads every slide and exercise before class: is the content correct, at the group's level, and does it practise the objective it maps to; wrong items are rewritten.
loop.stop: One draft per lesson; if the coordinator rejects it, they prepare the material.
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting text and exercises to a group's level needs rewriting, not a template.

steps.what: Instructional coordinator answers students' questions by e-mail

tasks.design: A lesson tool ({LMS}) drafts slides and exercises at the group's level from the lesson objectives; code checks each exercise maps to an objective, and the coordinator approves before class. A course FAQ answers routine questions on deadlines and materials. Teaching and advising students stay with the coordinator. No pupil data go into the drafting step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were rewritten by hand for each group.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson tools rewrite slide text by level and draft activities from objectives.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted material can be off level or dull.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing which student is lost and why.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator reviews drafts instead of preparing all material.

evidence.claim: LessonUp rewrites slide text by tone or level and translates.
In an NFER trial for the EEF, Oak's Aila cut lesson preparation by 49 minutes a week with quality no worse.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lesson plan to questions answered; assessment is outside.
Input contract: objectives set by the coordinator; fallback is preparing by hand.
Teaching and advising do not change.
Students read the FAQ in about the time an e-mail reply took.
research_questions: How much of the drafted material is kept?

incremental.description: Instructional coordinator keeps the course FAQ current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: stable lessons where drafts add little and students keep e-mailing (s3 90, s4 85) (2.5); high: new courses with many materials (8.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect material requests from teachers, compare materials and prices, decide and authorize purchases, place orders, track deliveries and budget, and tell teachers what has arrived.

steps.what: Teachers request materials on the purchasing system form
Instructional coordinator collects material requests from teachers by e-mail
Instructional coordinator compares materials and prices against district standards
Instructional coordinator recommends and authorizes purchase of instructional materials
Instructional coordinator orders materials from suppliers: by e-mail today; after the change the system builds the order from the authorized request
Instructional coordinator checks the order before it goes: items, quantities, prices, supplier and delivery address match the authorized request
Instructional coordinator releases the checked order to the supplier
Instructional coordinator tracks deliveries and budget in a spreadsheet
Instructional coordinator e-mails teachers that their materials have arrived: by hand today; after the change the system tells the requesting teacher when the coordinator marks the delivery received

tasks.design: Teachers request materials on a form in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}) that shows contracted suppliers' catalogues and prices, so requests arrive complete and comparable. Once the coordinator authorizes a request, the system builds the order; the coordinator checks it and releases it once to the supplier. Deliveries and budget show on a dashboard instead of a spreadsheet, and when the coordinator has checked a delivery the requesting teacher is notified. Choosing what fits students' needs stays with the coordinator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by e-mail in many formats and deliveries were tracked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Purchasing systems hold catalogues, approvals and delivery status.
tasks.still_hard: Special materials for pupils with support needs are often outside catalogues.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a reading series that pupils will actually like.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator authorizes and checks instead of collecting and typing.

evidence.claim: Purchasing systems handle request forms, catalogue prices, approvals and delivery status.

assumptions: Boundary: from teacher requests to teachers notified; supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: catalogues loaded by the school office; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheets.
Teachers fill the request form in about the time an e-mail took.

Authorizing stays with the coordinator and keeps its full time. The arrival notice is a fixed status message sent when the coordinator marks the delivery received in the purchasing system; that mark is an ordinary save, so it has no separate approval. Teachers' form requests (s0) replace their e-mails.
research_questions: Do materials arrive before the term starts more often?

incremental.description: Instructional coordinator adds non-catalogue items by hand.

approvals.approved_version: The order with items, quantities, prices and delivery address exactly as checked by the coordinator in s4a, sent once from the purchasing system to the named supplier; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many requests are special items outside the catalogues, so collecting, comparing and ordering stay partly by hand (s1 60, s2 80, s4 50) (38.3); high: most are standard catalogue orders (53.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scan industry developments and employer feedback, consult employers and teachers about changes, rewrite programme content and materials, check the updated programme with the team, and publish it.

steps.what: Internship employers rate how current the programme is on the yearly form
Instructional coordinator scans industry developments and employer feedback on equipment and processes
Instructional coordinator consults employers and teachers about changes
Instructional coordinator updates the content of educational programs to keep them technologically current

loop.input: The agreed changes, the current programme content and the learning outcomes.
loop.check: Code checks every learning outcome is still covered by a module and an assessment. The coordinator reads each drafted module against the agreed change: is the content correct and current, and is nothing dropped that the outcome needs; wrong parts are rewritten.
loop.stop: Stops when coverage passes and the coordinator approves, or after two failed redrafts the coordinator writes the module.
loop.why_not_simpler: New equipment and processes must be explained in prose; a coverage table alone does not.

steps.what: Instructional coordinator checks the updated programme with the teaching team
Instructional coordinator publishes the updated programme for students: by upload today, by one release from the course tool after the change

tasks.design: Internship employers rate how current the programme is on a short yearly form, and sector bodies' updates arrive as alerts in one feed, so the coordinator sees developments without searching. A course tool ({LMS}) drafts updated modules from the agreed changes and existing content; code checks every learning outcome stays covered, and the coordinator edits. Once the team has checked it, the coordinator releases the programme once to students. Consulting employers and teachers stays with the coordinator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Developments were followed by reading around and modules rewritten by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Course tools draft modules from existing material; employer feedback forms are easy to run.
tasks.still_hard: Schools rarely own the newest equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which new technique employers really use and which is hype.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator decides changes and edits drafts.

reach.learn: Whether interns arrive with current skills.

evidence.claim: Easygenerator drafts a course from slides or PDF documents.
Drafting course content is not an Annex III use; evaluating learning outcomes is.

assumptions: Boundary: from the programme review to the programme published; accreditation is outside.
Input contract: learning outcomes from the qualification file; fallback is rewriting by hand.
Employers fill the yearly form in about the time a call took.
Consulting and team checks do not change.
research_questions: Do employers rate the programme as more current?

incremental.description: Instructional coordinator runs the yearly employer form.

approvals.approved_version: The updated programme exactly as checked with the teaching team in s4, published once to the students' programme page in the course tool; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small updates where alerts and drafts add little (s1 90, s3 85) (11.1); high: a programme with many outdated modules (23.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The instructional coordinator keeps advising staff, teaching, choosing materials and deciding programme changes; e-mail answers, hand-written guides and spreadsheet tracking shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A coordinator with more time in classrooms.
